items.detail: Core PCE inflation rose to **3.3%** in October, above the 3.2% forecast, and the S&P 500 edged down 0.25% to 7,182.78 Wednesday.
items.why: Hotter inflation, plus third-quarter GDP growth of 4.3%, strengthened bets that the Fed keeps raising rates.

items.detail: The **Nasdaq** recovered from a drop of about 3.5% in the morning to close down 0.62% at 23,585.80, though Nvidia lost nearly 4% more.
items.why: A US plan for tariffs of up to 20% on 14 trading partners hit chips before buyers came back late.

items.detail: The **Dow** rose 0.33% to a record close of 50,182.95, and US stock markets are shut Thursday for Thanksgiving, with a half-day session Friday.
items.why: Investors kept moving money out of AI stocks and into defensive blue chips ahead of the holiday.

items.detail: Asian markets bounced back Thursday after Wednesday's rout, with Taiwan's Taiex up about **2.6%** and Hong Kong's Hang Seng up 1.9%.
items.why: Wall Street's late recovery eased panic over AI chips, though TSMC itself gained only 0.2%.

items.detail: The **Sensex** jumped 1,502 points to 83,938.28 Wednesday and added another 0.7% to around 84,520 by late Thursday morning, led by IT stocks.
items.why: Foreign buying, a stronger rupee and cheaper crude oil kept the rally going after the holiday break.

items.detail: The US **Russell 2000** rose 0.71% to 2,704.06 Wednesday, closing higher for a second day while the Nasdaq fell.
items.why: Easing pressure on AI stocks and the move into cheaper domestic companies offset worries about inflation and tariffs.

items.detail: **Bitcoin** got back above $60,000 late Wednesday, even as November's spot ETF outflows rose to a record **$4.94 billion**.
items.why: Traders betting on further falls were forced to buy back, while another $453 million left the ETFs.

items.detail: **Ether** hovered around **$1,685** Wednesday evening, holding near Tuesday's lows without recovering.
items.why: Spot ether ETFs keep losing money, with $314 million in outflows last week, which leaves little new demand.

items.detail: **Solana** rose about 1.2% to **$70.47** Wednesday, still holding above its $65 low.
items.why: Solana ETFs went back to small inflows, $0.7 million on Tuesday, while bitcoin and ether funds kept losing money.

items.detail: **Gold** fell to $3,426.71 Wednesday, its lowest in over a year, then rebounded about $160 to close near **$3,588**.
items.why: Hot inflation data fed rate-hike bets, then bargain hunters and the late stock recovery lifted gold before the holiday.

crossCuttingTheme: Hotter inflation and new US tariff threats hit chips, stocks and gold early Wednesday, then a late Wall Street recovery spread to Asian stocks, bitcoin and gold before Thanksgiving.
